title: Attorney General of Iowa

context.text: Neither primary was contested on June 2, 2026: Brenna Bird (R) received 181,319 votes and Nate Willems (D) 175,692.
Ballotpedia classifies the race as a battleground; Bird, first elected in 2022, was the first Republican to hold the office since 1979.
The Iowa Secretary of State's general-election candidate list (updated Aug. 19, 2026) shows only Bird (Republican) and Willems (Democratic) for Attorney General.

candidates.name: Brenna Bird
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the June 2 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Criminal justice: she says her office has doubled the number of prosecutors who handle murder, rape and child-molestation cases and has a dedicated cold-case unit.
Human trafficking and help for vulnerable victims.
Consumer protection, including her suit against crypto-ATM companies.

record.text: Announced a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging it harmed Iowa children, deceived parents and violated the Iowa Consumer Fraud Act.
Sued TP-Link Systems under the Iowa Consumer Fraud Act, alleging it deceived Iowans about the origin and safety of its routers and ties to China.
Led a bipartisan group of 30 attorneys general in a Supreme Court friend-of-the-court brief seeking to award 9/11 victims and families judgments from frozen Taliban funds.
Joined 43 states and territories seeking court approval of a $400 million settlement with Sandoz and Fougera over generic-drug pricing and competition.

candidates.researchNotes: Priorities are from Ballotpedia's summary of an Iowa's News Now interview; her campaign site was not read in detail. No direct statement on the guide's issue statements was found.

candidates.name: Nate Willems
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the June 2 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Hold corporations accountable when they break the law, including wage theft and price-raising practices, and hold polluters accountable.
Keep communities safe by holding criminals accountable, supporting first responders and helping crime victims.
Keep the office focused on Iowans' everyday concerns rather than personal political fights and national issues unrelated to Iowans.

record.text: Served on the Iowa House Education, Judiciary, Labor (vice chair) and State Government committees in 2009-2010 and as ranking member of Education in 2011-2012.

candidates.researchNotes: Legislative votes were not reviewed. His campaign says Bird is spending millions to mislead Iowans about his record; those claims were not evaluated.
